subject: baku
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: baku, the dream-eating tapir spirit.
Style: ukiyo-e woodblock print.

spec.name: Baku, Dream-Eating Spirit
spec.description: A stylised ukiyo-e woodblock-print baku: a tapir-bodied spirit with an elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, tiger paws and an ox tail, drawn in flat indigo, cream and vermilion with sumi outlines, spiral medallions, seigaiha waves and drifting dream-mist clouds at the tip of its trunk.
spec.layout: Stands on four legs facing +Z. Front to back: kasumi dream-mist clouds and glowing dream orbs (z 2.15 to 2.5), a trunk hanging from the snout and curling up at the tip (z 1.5 to 2.2), a tapir-shaped head with big round rhinoceros eyes and a white-tipped upper lip (z 1.0 to 1.55), a short thick neck with a flame-blade mane, a deep barrel torso (z -0.95 to 0.9, belly y 0.6, back y 1.38), a high rounded rump, and an ox tail with a tuft hanging behind (to z -1.45). Only the four tiger paws touch y = 0. Legs are short and sturdy with chunky paws. Ukiyo-e look: every surface is one flat colour with no shading tricks. Key shapes sit on a slightly larger sumi underlay so a bold dark outline shows. Colour comes in hard stepped bands (the bokashi gradient is three flat bands, never a blend). Pattern is built as small parts: vermilion spiral medallions on shoulders and haunches, a cream saddle cloth with seigaiha wave arcs, and cloud scrolls. The body is indigo, fore and hind quarters dark and the mid-body cream like a tapir. The palette is limited to woodblock pigments: indigo, vermilion, cream paper, ochre, sumi black.

parts.builds: Torso, neck and all the printed pattern on them. One loft or sweep body skinned over hips, spine1, spine2 and chest: deep barrel, half width about 0.4, height about 0.76 (belly y 0.6, back y 1.38), rump rounded and slightly higher than the withers. A short thick neck sweep over neck1 and neck2 (radius about 0.2 tapering to 0.16) ending inside the skull at headPivot. Colour in hard stepped bands, no blends. Fore and hind quarters are indigo (sectors), the mid-body is a wide cream (paper) tapir saddle with a sumi-outlined edge (a slightly larger sumi underlay strip, then the paper strip on top). The belly is a pale-blue (paleBlue) band below it, with a thin midBlue step between paleBlue and indigo. The neck is indigo with a paper throat band. On top of the body: a woven saddle cloth in deepRed with a gold trim border over the paper saddle (a flat box or loft bulging only slightly), carrying a seigaiha (blue-wave) pattern of 3 to 4 concentric arcs per wave, in waveWhite, midBlue and indigo, as small flat half-rings (thin cylinders or sweeps, each about 3 cm) in overlapping rows. A shimenawa-style rope (twisted ochre and paper sweeps) loops round the girth with 4 vermilion tassels and tiny paper zigzag shide on it. Spiral medallions in vermilion with cream centres and sumi outlines (swept spiral paths, about 0.2 m across) seated on the shoulder at (±0.4, 1.05, 0.5) and the haunch at (±0.4, 1.05, -0.6), the signature karashishi swirl motif. Sumi outline pieces on the chest and rump. A cream cloud-scroll (kasumi) band along the flank, each cloud a flat scalloped extrude. Rump: tail root plug in indigo at tailRoot. Bone: put pieces on the nearest of hips, spine1, spine2, chest, neck1, neck2.
parts.attaches: Hind legs hang from hipL and hipR (hips); front legs from shoulderL and shoulderR (chest); neck sweep ends at headPivot and the head part continues from it; tail begins at tailRoot; the extras part's mane rides the neck and back from maneStart to maneEnd and sits on the surface.

parts.builds: Head, trunk, jaws, ears, tusks and face. Skull is a tapir wedge: braincase about 0.36 wide and 0.4 tall from z 1.0 to 1.3, tapering to a broad snout. The upper jaw and snout is its own piece in indigo with a paper-white lip tip (tapir white lip) outlined in sumi. Lower jaw is a separate piece on joint jaw (z 1.2 to 1.5, under the snout), indigo with a paper chin and a row of small ivory teeth; the mouth can open. Elephant trunk: a thick sweep over trunk1..trunk4 and trunkTip, root radius 0.11 tapering to 0.05, from trunkRoot hanging down and curling up at trunkTip. Cream ring ribs every 6 cm as thin torus or sweep rings, paper underside stripe (sector), two nose-hole discs in nose colour at the tip, and a vermilion band cuff halfway. Two ivory tusks curl up from the upper lip beside the trunk root. Rhinoceros eyes: big round eyes at eyeL and eyeR (radius about 0.055) built in layers: a sumi underlay disc, an eyeGold iris, a vermilion ring, a sumi slit pupil and a small waveWhite highlight; heavy indigo brow ridges above, with rose-and-sumi lashes or brow flicks in ukiyo-e line style. A vermilion tomoe (comma) emblem on the forehead at foreheadEmblem, outlined in sumi and gold. Round ears on joints earL and earR: indigo outer disc, paper rim, a rose inner disc and a few ochre fur tufts. Cheek ruffs of 5 to 6 overlapping flame-blade shapes in indigo, midBlue and paper on each side. Everything is flat colour with an outline underlay layer beneath the key shapes.
parts.attaches: Skull base meets the neck sweep at headPivot (head joint). The jaw hinges at jawHinge. The trunk starts at trunkRoot and ends at trunkTip. Ears root at earRootL and earRootR. The mane begins just behind the skull at maneStart; nothing of the head part lies behind z 0.95.

parts.builds: All four legs, short and sturdy, with chunky tiger paws. Front legs are sweeps skinned over shoulder, elbow and wrist joints (radius about 0.11 to 0.075); hind legs are skinned over hip, knee, hock and foot (thicker thigh about 0.16, hock bending back). Legs are indigo with a midBlue step on the lower leg and paper socks. Each foot is a big rounded tiger paw (a squashed sphere or capsule about 0.15 wide) in paper with a sumi outline underlay, four toes as small paper spheres or capsules, a rose pad under it, and four ivory claws peeking out in front. Paw soles rest on y = 0 (sink at most 2 cm). Vermilion garter bands with gold studs at each wrist and hock, with a small cloud-curl tuft above them. Fur ruffs at elbow and hock made of 4 to 5 overlapping flame-blade extrudes in indigo, midBlue and paper. A small vermilion spiral on the outer upper hind thigh. Thighs and shoulders tuck into the torso volume, so no gaps show. Put pieces on the leg joints of their own side, mirrored for x-positive L and x-negative R.
parts.attaches: Front legs start at shoulderL and shoulderR on the chest, hind legs at hipL and hipR on the hips, buried into the torso. Foot centres are at x of plus or minus 0.3, y 0.07, z 0.6 (front) and z -0.62 (hind). The body part's shoulder and haunch spirals sit just above and outside them.

parts.builds: Mane, tail and dream mist. Mane: a crest of broad overlapping flame-blade extrudes (ukiyo-e wind-swept hair) from maneStart down the neck and along the spine to maneEnd, each about 0.15 to 0.3 long leaning backward, in a root-to-tip palette of deepIndigo, indigo, midBlue, paper, with a vermilion tip on every third blade, over a solid indigo ridge sweep; a few gold-edged curls at the base of the skull. Ox tail on tail1..tail4: indigo tapering sweep (radius 0.06 to 0.035) with a big tuft at the end made of 8 to 10 overlapping flame blades in indigo, paper and vermilion tips, plus a gold band at the tuft base. Dream mist (the dreams the baku eats): around dreamOrigin, in front of trunkTip at z 2.15 to 2.5, within x plus or minus 0.45 and y 0.85 to 1.95 (never on the floor, nothing touching the legs). Four flat kasumi clouds made of scalloped extrudes (waveWhite, paleBlue, rose, each with a thin sumi or midBlue offset underlay for the outline), stacked in loose bands. Three or four dream orbs (dreamGlow, dreamViolet, vermilion spheres of radius 0.04 to 0.07, with tiny waveWhite highlights), some with swirling spiral tails. A thin spiral wisp sweep in dreamViolet and waveWhite flows from the clouds into the trunk tip. Use the glow kit on the orbs and a few wisp pieces. All details are small seated parts in their own flat colours. Put the mane on the neck1, neck2, chest, spine joints, the tail on the tail joints, and the mist on trunkTip or the root.
parts.attaches: Mane sits on the neck and back surface from maneStart to maneEnd, just behind the head's skull. The tail roots at tailRoot on joint tail1, continuing the rump plug. Mist hovers at dreamOrigin just beyond trunkTip, and its wisp ends at trunkTip, touching the trunk.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching the baku's design, drawing on the traditional elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, ox tail, tiger paws, and bear body, sized like a tapir but exaggerated for fantasy. I'm planning the ukiyo-e aesthetic too—flat color blocks of indigo and vermilion against cream paper, bold black outlines, and wave motifs.

Now I'm breaking the creature into body parts (torso with tapir markings, trunk-snout head with tusks and mane, tiger-pawed legs, ox tail with dream-mist wisps near the snout) and laying out joint positions and proportions in model space for the standing pose.

I'll use the tentacle role for the trunk chain, hinge for the ears, and tail role for the tail joints branching from the hips. For legs I'm sketching a front chain of shoulder, elbow, and paw, and a hind chain of hip, knee, hock, and foot, deciding how much joint detail to include per limb.

Toes as rigid parts on the paw joint, fine. Now I'm splitting the budget across four parts: body (with markings and a decorative saddle cloth using seigaiha patterns and a tassel rope), head, legs, and a combined tail/mane/dream part carrying the flame-like neck crest, back mane, tail, and the dream clouds and orbs near the trunk. Boxes can overlap slightly between parts sitting on each other, which should be acceptable.

I'm figuring out sizing for that extras box: tail tip back to around -1.45, dream mist wisps curling off the trunk up to about z 2.35, giving a length near 3.8, with heights reaching roughly 1.65-1.9 for the head/ears, mane, and dream clouds respectively, while legs stay grounded on the floor.

Now I'm defining mount points — neck base, head pivot, jaw hinge, trunk root, ear roots, shoulders, hips, tail root, mane start, dream origin near the trunk tip, and saddle top — then laying out a ukiyo-e inspired palette with cream paper tones, prussian and deep indigo, vermilion, sumi black, ochre, pale blue, moss green, wave white, and rose pink.

For the baku's coloring I'm settling on an indigo body for the fore and hindquarters with a pale blue-white belly, a cream saddle band outlined in sumi ink, and vermilion kasumi cloud-scroll patterns accenting the shoulder and haunch like tiger markings.

I'm adding spiral karashishi-style medallions at the shoulders and haunches in vermilion and cream, with bold sumi outlines around each shape and flat solid color fields throughout. The saddle cloth gets a seigaiha wave pattern of concentric arcs, and I'm simulating bokashi gradients using 2-3 stepped color bands going from pale belly to mid-tone to full indigo, keeping everything built from flat, gradient-free color fields that reference named palette swatches.

Now I'm working out the skeletal ownership: body part handles the torso loft from hips to chest and the neck sweep up to the head joint, head part owns the skull forward of that joint, and mane sits as a separate extras piece along neck and back. I'm sketching out joint positions and sizes for the head and ears, mirroring left/right sides with sign-flipped coordinates.

Now I'm placing the tapir's distinctive low-held head, defining the skull box, jaw joint and small lower jaw beneath the trunk, and plotting the drooping proboscis as a chain of trunk segments hanging down from the upper face.

Finishing the trunk tip near [0,1.06,2.2] with mist trailing further out, giving an overall body length around 4.0 units. Now I'm blocking out the torso proportions — rump and chest positions, barrel radius and height — plus setting ear/mane height and shoulder position for the front legs.

Now I'm planning the full joint hierarchy: hips as root, then spine, chest, neck, head, jaw, ears, trunk segments, tail segments, and both front and rear leg chains down to the paws, keeping names alphanumeric with no underscores. I'm mapping which joints parent to which — shoulders off the chest, hind legs off the hips, trunk off the head — and noting ear direction vectors before moving into writing the actual mount/part definitions.

Starting the body part with a torso loft, belly bands, neck sweep, chest, a saddle cloth decorated with seigaiha pattern, rope and tassel details, spiral medallions at the shoulders and haunches, kasumi cloud bands, and the rump, budgeted at 230 primitives with joints from hips through neck2. Then the head part brings skull and brow ridges styled like rhino eyes with sumi outlines and vermilion pupil rings, a trunk built from ribbed rings, nostrils, and an upper jaw with a tapir-style white tip.

Continuing with the lower jaw, tusks, teeth, round ears with cream rims, a forehead emblem with a vermilion tomoe, and whiskers, budgeted at 230 with joints for head, jaw, ears, and a trunk chain. For the legs I'm planning tiger paws with toes and claws, fur ruffs, vermilion garters, and leg wraps with cloud cuffs, budgeted at 220 with the hind leg hips set back and thigh volume tucked under the body. Now I'm starting on the extras, beginning with a flame-shaped mane or crest running from neck to back.

Extending that into blade-like mane segments shading from indigo at the root to vermilion to cream at the tip, plus an ox tail with a tuft, and dreamlike kasumi cloud bands and glowing orbs floating at the trunk tip -- budgeted at 200, using neck/spine joints for the mane and tail joints for the tail, with a bounding box wide enough to contain the floating mist elements above floor level. Tallying everything up, the total budget comes to 900 across all four parts, which checks out. I'm also thinking the dream mist could clutter the composition, so I want to describe it more precisely as three or four flat kasumi cloud bands.

Now I'm refining the mist details: scalloped outline cloud bands in cream and pale blue floating above and in front of the trunk tip, with three small orbs and a spiral wisp swept into it, keeping everything bounded tightly around the trunk's position. Writing the JSON now, keeping the palette to 24 names or fewer...
